title: Google’s satellite AI server transmits its first response to Earth
slides: Google's satellite AI just answered Earth — why now?
The model runs entirely in orbit, no ground link needed
But it can only process what its sensors capture first
Disaster response teams could get answers before downlink
Ask: who controls the model above your head?
thread_text:
1. AI Just Left Earth

A satellite just ran a full AI model in orbit, no ground link needed. That means decisions about what's happening on the ground could be made 500 km above your head.

2. Why Orbit Changes Everything

The model processes data on the spot, cutting the delay from hours to seconds. Disaster teams could get answers before the satellite even downlinks.

3. The Sensor Bottleneck

It can only analyze what its own eyes see. No ground truth, no extra data — just what the satellite's instruments captured first.

4. Who's Watching the Watcher?

No human in the loop for the first pass. That raises a simple question: who audits the model when it's out of reach?

5. Your Move

Next time you hear 'AI in space', ask: who controls the model above your head? If you can't answer, that's the problem.
